Given the projection of \(\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}\) onto a vector \(\mathbf{w}\) is \(\begin{pmatrix} -9/10 \\ 3/10 \end{pmatrix}\), we need to find the projection of \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}\) onto \(\mathbf{w}\).

First, we determine the direction of \(\mathbf{w}\). The projection formula gives us:
\[
\text{proj}_{\mathbf{w}} \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -9/10 \\ 3/10 \end{pmatrix}
\]
This projection is a scalar multiple of \(\mathbf{w}\). By solving the equations derived from the projection formula, we find that \(\mathbf{w}\) is in the direction of \(\begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}\).

Next, we use the projection formula to find the projection of \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}\) onto \(\mathbf{w}\). The projection matrix \(P\) onto \(\mathbf{w}\) is:
\[
P = \frac{1}{10} \begin{pmatrix} 9 & -3 \\ -3 & 1 \end{pmatrix}
\]

Applying this projection matrix to \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}\):
\[
P \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{10} \begin{pmatrix} 9 & -3 \\ -3 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{10} \begin{pmatrix} 33 \\ -11 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 33/10 \\ -11/10 \end{pmatrix}
\]

Thus, the projection of \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}\) onto \(\mathbf{w}\) is:
\[
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix} \dfrac{33}{10} \\ -\dfrac{11}{10} \end{pmatrix}}
\]
